about: The emulator's own conformance stimuli (scripts/conformance.py, format in scripts/s32case.py). Each runs on the firmware directory you supply (make firmware writes one for the stock v86 images) and must give a byte-identical canonical trace on every build. They exercise the hardware model, not any firmware behaviour: no case judges what the firmware does. A firmware project adds its own cases through --provider (docs/conformance.md).

cases.name: first-power-up
cases.about: every configuration chip blank: the firmware's first power-up writes its defaults (FRAM write path)

cases.name: boot-home
cases.about: power-on to the Controller's home page and 2 s after it, engine stopped

cases.name: cruise
cases.about: 2400 RPM, MAP and TPS counts, four cylinders (the default configuration)

cases.name: rpm-profile
cases.about: start, run-up, cut: engine speed steps and crank-sensor jitter

cases.name: sensor-faults
cases.about: crank glitch and drop, MAP short, TPS noise, ET open

cases.name: power-and-link
cases.about: ECU2 breaker off and on, a dead link to ECU1, supply sag, retard switch

cases.name: bezel
cases.about: menu, knob and encoder input after the home page (button debounce, encoder steps)

cases.name: ct-sd-card
cases.about: a card in the Controller's slot with one text file (SD over SPI, FAT32)

cases.name: fram-carry
cases.about: the configuration chips the first power-up wrote, in the next power-up (case: sources)
